response.sql: SELECT SUM(rebtotal) AS total_rebate, AVG(feerate - rebrate) AS avg_net_fee_rate FROM fees WHERE rebrate >= 0.0005;

assumptions.assumption: Each fee record is one row of the fees table, so no join is needed. Rows with a NULL rebrate fail the filter and are excluded. SUM and AVG skip NULLs, so missing values are ignored, and the result is NULL when nothing aggregates. No rounding is applied.
The average net fee rate is the mean of the per-row difference feerate - rebrate. A row with a NULL feerate or rebrate has a NULL difference and is left out of that average.

alternatives.interpretation: Average net fee rate read as the average feerate minus the average rebrate over the same filtered rows. This matches the primary query when no values are missing, but the two averages can cover different row sets when feerate or rebrate has NULLs.
alternatives.sql: SELECT SUM(rebtotal) AS total_rebate, AVG(feerate) - AVG(rebrate) AS avg_net_fee_rate FROM fees WHERE rebrate >= 0.0005;
